summary: Godabarish Mishra was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Ravenshaw College (~1906–1910) and the University of Calcutta (~1910–1912). He taught at Satyabadi Bana Bidyalaya (1913–1919), was headmaster at Chakradharpur High School (1919–1921), and directed at the University of Madras.

Gombojab Tsybikov was a scholar in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tomsk State University (~1893–1895) and Saint Petersburg State University (1895–1899), later serving at the Oriental Institute, Vladivostok (~1902–1917) and Far Eastern Federal University (~1918–1922).

Gopal Lal Meena is an Indologist who taught Shagun Sinha. His career includes posts as a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University and professor emeritus at the University of Delhi (both attested 2026).

Gopinath Kaviraj worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under Arthur Venis, Madhusudan Ojha, and Shashadhar Tarkachuramani, and at Allahabad and Maharani College. He served Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as librarian (1914–1920), principal (1923–1937), and Yoga-Tantra head (1964–1969).

Gordon Dester Kaufman was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Bethel College, Northwestern University, and Yale University. He held posts at Pomona College, Vanderbilt University, and Harvard University as Mallinckrodt Professor of Divinity from 1963.

Gordon Hannington Luce was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who was educated at Dean Close School and the University of Cambridge (~1908–1911). He served as a professor at the University of Rangoon from around 1923 to 1964.

Gordon Johnson is an Indologist and historian who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1961–1967). He served as a fellow of Trinity and Selwyn Colleges, president of Wolfson College (1993–2010), Cambridge's Deputy Vice-Chancellor (1974–2010), and president of the Royal Asiatic Society (2015–2018).

Gore Ouseley worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held a post at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (~1810–1814) and served as vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1844).

Gottfried Bernhardy was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. Educated at the Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1817–1822), he held a long-term academic post at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from approximately 1829 to 1875.

Gottfried Ernst Groddeck was a linguistics and history scholar who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (~1782–1786) and Danzig. He held academic posts at Vilnius University (~1798–1803) and the Imperial University of Vilna (~1803–1824).

Gottfried Hermann was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and the University of Jena. He spent his career at Leipzig, serving as extraordinary professor of philosophy from 1798 and director of the philological seminar from 1803 to 1848.

Gottfried Kinkel was a scholar in the field of history and archaeology. After studying at the University of Bonn (~1831–1834), he held positions at Bonn (~1837–1849) and later at ETH Zurich (~1866–1882).

Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Königsberg (~1710–1716) and under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts at Königsberg schools, the University of Königsberg (~1717–1725), and the Russian Academy of Sciences (1726).

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at King's College London and Heidelberg. He held posts at King's College, was principal of Government College University, Lahore (1864), and was registrar of the University of the Punjab.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served on the faculty as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin from approximately 1974 to 1993.

Govind Chandra Pande was a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as vice-chancellor of the University of Allahabad and University of Rajasthan, visiting professor at BHU, and chairman of the IIAS and Allahabad Museum.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and completed his PhD at Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He served as head of sociology at the University of Mumbai (1924–1959).

Govind Swamirao Gai was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India (attested 1958–1967) and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and as an epigraphy consultant for the AIIS.

Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indologist who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. His career included posts as professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who held academic positions as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).
